name: FirstUK Bank Escalation Matrix
description: The formal escalation matrix governing how operational issues, complaints, and exceptions are routed through defined authority levels at FirstUK Bank. Effective from 2026-01-15, owned by the Chief Operating Officer and applicable across all staff, management, and executive levels.

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Executive-level role responsible for ownership and governance of the escalation matrix at FirstUK Bank.

name: Operations Department
description: Department responsible for maintaining and administering the escalation matrix procedures.

name: Escalation Matrix Process
description: An end-to-end operational procedure that defines clear escalation paths for issues, incidents, and decisions based on severity, type, and financial impact. The process ensures rapid resolution, appropriate authority, and transparent accountability throughout the escalation chain.
context: The Escalation Matrix defines clear escalation paths for issues, incidents, and decisions based on severity, type, and financial impact.
Ensures rapid resolution, appropriate authority, and transparent accountability.

name: Level 1 — Frontline Resolution
description: The first escalation tier handling routine customer service issues with an approval limit of less than £500. Managed by Customer Service Staff, Branch Staff, and Account Managers, this level resolves account inquiries, fee reversals, product inquiries, card replacements, and password resets within 24 hours. Issues that remain unresolved or are deemed complex are escalated to Level 2.
context: Authority: Customer Service Staff, Branch Staff, Account Managers
Escalation Condition: If customer unhappy or issue complex → Escalate to Level 2

name: Customer Service Staff
description: Frontline personnel responsible for handling Level 1 escalation issues including account inquiries, fee reversals, product inquiries, and password resets within the <£500 approval limit.
context: Authority: Customer Service Staff, Branch Staff, Account Managers

name: Branch Staff
description: Branch-based personnel with Level 1 escalation authority to resolve customer service issues up to £500, including account inquiries, fee reversals, and card replacements.
context: Authority: Customer Service Staff, Branch Staff, Account Managers

name: Account Manager
description: Account management personnel with Level 1 escalation authority to approve resolutions up to £500 for customer service issues including inquiries, fee reversals, and product information.
context: Authority: Customer Service Staff, Branch Staff, Account Managers

name: Customer Satisfaction and Issue Complexity Gate
description: A decision gate at Level 1 that determines whether an issue can be resolved at the frontline or must be escalated to Level 2. The gate triggers escalation if the customer remains unhappy or if the issue is deemed complex.
context: Escalation Condition: If customer unhappy or issue complex → Escalate to Level 2

name: Level 2 — Supervisor/Manager Resolution
description: Second-tier escalation level handling complaint investigations, non-standard fee reversals, account exceptions, and customer retention offers. Staffed by supervisors, branch managers, and complaints handlers with authority to approve decisions up to £5,000. Targets resolution within 1–3 business days and escalates unresolved cases or those exceeding £5,000 impact to Level 3.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler
If unresolved or >£5k impact → Escalate to Level 3

name: Supervisor
description: Staff member with authority to resolve Level 2 escalations, including complaint investigations and account exception handling, with approval limits up to £5,000.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Branch Manager
description: Senior branch staff member with authority to resolve Level 2 escalations, including complaint investigations and customer retention offers, with approval limits up to £5,000.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Complaints Handler
description: Specialist staff member responsible for investigating complaints and handling account exceptions at Level 2, with approval authority up to £5,000.
context: Authority: Supervisor, Branch Manager, Complaints Handler

name: Level 2 Escalation Trigger — Unresolved or High-Impact Case
description: Decision gate at Level 2 determining whether a case is resolved within authority limits or escalated to Level 3. Escalation is triggered if the case remains unresolved or the financial impact exceeds £5,000.
context: If unresolved or >£5k impact → Escalate to Level 3

name: Level 3 — Department Head Resolution
description: Third escalation tier for complaint and exception resolution, with authority over decisions valued between £5,000 and £50,000. Handles significant complaints, regulatory exceptions, high-value fraud investigations, product exceptions, vendor disputes, and AML/KYC escalations involving high-risk customers. Requires resolution within 3–5 business days.
context: Authority: Department Head (e.g., Head of Retail Banking, Head of Compliance)

name: Department Head
description: Senior operational authority responsible for resolving escalated complaints, regulatory exceptions, high-value fraud investigations, product exceptions, vendor disputes, and AML/KYC decisions at Level 3. Examples include Head of Retail Banking and Head of Compliance.
context: Authority: Department Head (e.g., Head of Retail Banking, Head of Compliance)

name: Escalation Trigger — Level 3 to Level 4
description: Decision gate at Level 3 that determines whether an issue is resolved or escalated further to Level 4. Escalation is triggered if the matter remains unresolved or the financial impact exceeds £50,000.
context: Escalation Condition: If unresolved or >£50k impact → Escalate to Level 4

name: Level 4 — Executive Resolution
description: Fourth escalation tier referenced as the next level when Level 3 issues remain unresolved or exceed £50,000 in financial impact.
context: If unresolved or >£50k impact → Escalate to Level 4

name: Significant Complaint Resolution
description: Department Head-level decision to resolve significant customer complaints involving substantial refunds, escalated from lower tiers.

name: Regulatory Exception Request
description: Department Head-level approval of requests for exceptions to regulatory or policy requirements, escalated for senior authority.

name: High-Value Fraud Investigation
description: Investigation of significant fraud cases escalated to Department Head level for resolution and decision-making.

name: Product Exception Request
description: Department Head-level approval of requests for exceptions to standard product terms or conditions.

name: Vendor/Partnership Dispute Resolution Authority
description: Department Head authority responsible for resolving vendor and partnership disputes escalated to Level 3.

name: AML/KYC High-Risk Customer Decision
description: Department Head-level decision on Anti-Money Laundering and Know Your Customer matters involving high-risk customers, escalated from lower tiers.

name: Level 4 — Executive Committee Resolution
description: The fourth escalation tier for unresolved issues or high-impact matters requiring executive decision-making. Authority vested in CEO, CFO, CRO, and COO with approval limits between £50,000 and £500,000. Response time is 24–48 hours, with further escalation to the Board triggered if the matter remains unresolved or impact exceeds £500,000.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)
If unresolved or >£500k impact → Escalate to Level 5 (Board)

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive member of the escalation Level 4 committee with authority to approve resolutions for matters valued between £50,000 and £500,000.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)

name: Chief Financial Officer
description: Executive member of the escalation Level 4 committee with authority to approve resolutions for matters valued between £50,000 and £500,000.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive member of the escalation Level 4 committee with authority to approve resolutions for matters valued between £50,000 and £500,000.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Executive member of the escalation Level 4 committee with authority to approve resolutions for matters valued between £50,000 and £500,000.
context: Authority: CEO, CFO, CRO, COO (Executive Committee)

name: Executive Committee Escalation Trigger
description: Decision gate determining whether an issue requires Executive Committee resolution at Level 4 or further escalation to the Board. Triggered by major financial loss exceeding £50,000, significant regulatory breach, reputational crisis, major vendor issue, strategic exception, or large fraud investigation.

name: Board Escalation Threshold
description: Decision gate determining whether an unresolved Level 4 matter or one with impact exceeding £500,000 must be escalated to the Board (Level 5) for final resolution.
context: If unresolved or >£500k impact → Escalate to Level 5 (Board)

name: Level 5 — Board Resolution
description: The highest escalation tier requiring Board of Directors approval for decisions exceeding £500,000 or involving critical regulatory breaches, reputational crises, legal liabilities, strategic decisions, license/charter risks, or systemic operational failures. Response time is 24–72 hours with emergency meeting capability for urgent matters.
context: Response Time: 24–72 hours (emergency meeting if urgent)

name: Board of Directors
description: The governing authority responsible for approving escalations at Level 5, with decision-making authority over matters exceeding £500,000 and critical organizational risks including regulatory breaches, reputational crises, and systemic failures.

name: Customer Complaint Resolution Process
description: An issue-specific escalation procedure for handling customer complaints across three severity levels (Low, High, Critical), with defined initial handlers, escalation timelines, and regulatory notification requirements. The process routes complaints through escalation levels 1–5 depending on severity, financial impact, and regulatory implications.
context: If unresolved: Escalate to Complaints Manager (Level 3)

name: Initial Complaint Receipt and Severity Assessment
description: The first step in which a complaint is received and classified by severity level (Low, High, or Critical) to determine the appropriate initial handler and escalation pathway.

name: Low Severity Complaint Handling
description: Resolution of minor service issues by Customer Service Staff within 24 hours, with escalation to Complaints Manager (Level 3) if unresolved.

name: High Severity Complaint Handling
description: Resolution of significant financial loss complaints by Complaints Manager within 24–48 hours, with Compliance notification and Board notification if loss exceeds £100k.

name: Critical Severity Complaint Handling
description: Immediate handling of regulatory or reputational breaches by Head of Customer Service and Compliance Head within 24 hours, with mandatory FCA notification and immediate Board escalation.
context: Initial Handler: Head of Customer Service + Compliance Head

name: Compliance Notification
description: Notification of Compliance function when a High Severity complaint involves regulatory implications, ensuring regulatory oversight of complaint resolution.

name: Board Notification for High-Value Loss
description: Escalation to Board when a High Severity complaint involves financial loss exceeding £100k, ensuring executive awareness of material financial impact.

name: FCA Notification
description: Notification to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) within 24 hours when a Critical Severity complaint involves regulatory requirements, ensuring compliance with regulatory notification obligations.

name: Immediate Board Notification for Critical Issues
description: Immediate notification to the Board when a Critical Severity complaint is identified, ensuring executive awareness of regulatory or reputational breaches.

name: Customer Service Staff
description: The frontline role responsible for receiving and initially handling Low Severity complaints within 24 hours, with authority to resolve minor service issues or escalate to Complaints Manager.

name: Complaints Manager
description: The escalation point for unresolved Low Severity complaints and the initial handler for High Severity complaints, responsible for resolution within 24–48 hours and coordination with Compliance.
context: If unresolved: Escalate to Complaints Manager (Level 3)

name: Head of Customer Service
description: Senior leadership role jointly responsible with Compliance Head for handling Critical Severity complaints involving regulatory or reputational breaches, with authority to escalate to Board and FCA.
context: Initial Handler: Head of Customer Service + Compliance Head

name: Compliance Head
description: Senior compliance leadership role jointly responsible with Head of Customer Service for handling Critical Severity complaints, ensuring regulatory compliance and coordinating FCA notification.
context: Initial Handler: Head of Customer Service + Compliance Head

name: Compliance Function
description: The compliance function notified when High Severity complaints have regulatory implications, responsible for ensuring regulatory oversight and compliance with notification obligations.

name: Board
description: The Board receives notification when High Severity complaints involve financial loss exceeding £100k and receives immediate notification for all Critical Severity complaints.

name: Financial Conduct Authority
description: The external regulatory authority notified within 24 hours when Critical Severity complaints involve regulatory requirements, as mandated by regulatory obligations.

name: Complaint Severity Classification
description: The initial decision point that classifies a complaint as Low, High, or Critical severity, determining the appropriate initial handler, escalation level, timeline, and regulatory notification requirements.

name: Low Severity Resolution Check
description: A decision point at 24 hours to determine whether a Low Severity complaint has been resolved by Customer Service Staff or requires escalation to Complaints Manager (Level 3).
context: If unresolved: Escalate to Complaints Manager (Level 3)

name: Financial Loss Threshold Check
description: A decision point for High Severity complaints to determine whether financial loss exceeds £100k, triggering mandatory Board notification.

name: Regulatory Notification Requirement Check
description: A decision point for Critical Severity complaints to determine whether regulatory notification to the FCA is required within 24 hours.

name: Level 1 — Customer Service Staff Resolution
description: The frontline escalation level for Low Severity complaints, handled by Customer Service Staff with a 24-hour resolution timeline.

name: Level 2 — Customer Service Staff Escalation
description: The second escalation level for Low Severity complaints, still within Customer Service Staff authority, before escalation to Complaints Manager.

name: Level 3 — Complaints Manager Resolution
description: The escalation point for unresolved Low Severity complaints and the initial level for High Severity complaints, handled by Complaints Manager with 24–48 hour timeline and Compliance notification.
context: If unresolved: Escalate to Complaints Manager (Level 3)

name: Level 4 — Senior Management Resolution
description: The escalation level for High Severity complaints and initial level for Critical Severity complaints, involving senior management with 24–48 hour timeline for High Severity and 24 hours for Critical.

name: Level 5 — Executive and Regulatory Escalation
description: The highest escalation level for Critical Severity complaints, involving Head of Customer Service and Compliance Head with 24-hour timeline, immediate Board notification, and FCA notification within 24 hours.

name: Complaint Originator
description: The customer who initiates a complaint regarding a service issue, financial loss, or regulatory/reputational breach, triggering the complaint resolution process.

name: Fraud Incident Response Process
description: End-to-end procedure for detecting, investigating, and resolving fraud incidents across three severity tiers based on fraud amount. The process defines handler roles, escalation levels, investigation timelines, reimbursement obligations, and regulatory reporting requirements.

name: Fraud Investigation and Blocking
description: Initial investigation step for low-value fraud incidents under £1,000. Includes assessment of ongoing fraud activity and blocking of transactions or accounts if necessary.
context: Action: Investigate, block if ongoing, reimburse if customer fraud

name: Fraud Investigation with Law Enforcement Contact
description: Investigation step for mid-range fraud incidents between £1,000–£10,000. Includes potential contact with law enforcement authorities when warranted by the investigation findings.

name: Investigation with Law Enforcement Notification and Board Update
aliases: Investigation, law enforcement notification, Board update
description: Investigation step for high-value fraud incidents exceeding £10,000. Includes mandatory law enforcement notification and escalation to Board level with regulatory reporting considerations.
context: Action: Investigation, law enforcement notification, Board update

name: Customer Reimbursement Processing
description: Reimbursement step executed for confirmed customer fraud cases. Low-value incidents are reimbursed immediately; mid and high-value incidents are reimbursed within 10 days.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Team responsible for investigating fraud incidents across low and mid-range severity tiers (under £10,000). Handles initial investigation, blocking decisions, and law enforcement coordination for incidents between £1,000–£10,000.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Senior executive responsible for handling mid-range and high-value fraud incidents. Participates in investigation and decision-making for incidents £1,000–£10,000 and above £10,000.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive-level authority responsible for high-value fraud incidents exceeding £10,000. Participates in investigation decisions and Board-level updates.

name: Level 2 — Financial Crime Team Fraud Response
description: First escalation tier for fraud incidents under £1,000. Handled by Financial Crime Team with 24-hour response timeline and authority to investigate and block ongoing fraud.

name: Level 3 — Financial Crime Team and CRO Fraud Response
description: Mid-range escalation tier for fraud incidents between £1,000–£10,000. Handled jointly by Financial Crime Team and CRO with 24-hour response timeline, law enforcement contact authority, and 10-day reimbursement obligation.

name: Level 4–5 — CRO and CEO Fraud Response
description: High-value escalation tier for fraud incidents exceeding £10,000. Handled by CRO and CEO with 4-hour response timeline, mandatory law enforcement notification, Board update requirement, and potential regulatory SAR filing.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory compliance gate for high-value fraud incidents exceeding £10,000. Determines whether a Suspicious Activity Report must be filed with the relevant authority based on investigation findings.

name: Low-Value Fraud Alert
description: Fraud detection alert for incidents under £1,000. Triggers investigation and potential blocking by Financial Crime Team with 24-hour response requirement.
context: Action: Investigate, block if ongoing, reimburse if customer fraud

name: Mid-Range Fraud Alert
description: Fraud detection alert for incidents between £1,000–£10,000. Triggers joint investigation by Financial Crime Team and CRO with law enforcement contact authority and 10-day reimbursement timeline.
context: Action: Investigation + law enforcement contact (if warranted)

name: High-Value Fraud Alert
description: Fraud detection alert for incidents exceeding £10,000. Triggers executive-level investigation by CRO and CEO with mandatory law enforcement notification, Board update, and potential regulatory SAR filing within 4-hour response window.
context: Action: Investigation, law enforcement notification, Board update

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing Obligation
description: Regulatory obligation to file a Suspicious Activity Report with the relevant authority for high-value fraud incidents exceeding £10,000 when investigation findings warrant reporting.

name: Operational Incidents and System Outages Management
description: End-to-end procedure for managing operational incidents and system outages, with escalation tiers based on duration and customer impact. The process defines handler responsibilities, escalation triggers, communication requirements, and regulatory notification obligations across three severity levels.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Incident Logging and Initial Assessment
description: Initial step where operational incidents are logged and assessed for duration and customer impact. This step determines the severity tier and whether escalation is required.
context: Log incident, no escalation if <1 hour

name: Short Duration Incident Resolution
description: Resolution pathway for incidents lasting less than 1 hour with minimal customer impact. Handled by IT Operations with no escalation required.

name: Medium Duration Incident Resolution and Escalation
description: Resolution pathway for incidents lasting 1–4 hours with significant customer impact. Handled by IT Operations and CTO, with escalation to CRO and COO after 2 hours and customer communication if duration exceeds 2 hours.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Long Duration Incident Resolution and Executive Escalation
description: Resolution pathway for incidents lasting more than 4 hours with critical customer impact. Handled by CTO and CEO with immediate response, hourly updates, executive committee meeting, potential FCA notification, and board update if duration exceeds 8 hours.

name: Incident Duration Classification Gate
description: Branching decision point that classifies incidents into three severity tiers based on duration: <1 hour (minimal impact), 1–4 hours (significant impact), or >4 hours (critical impact). Each path triggers different handler assignments, escalation timelines, and communication protocols.

name: Two-Hour Escalation Trigger
description: Decision point within the 1–4 hour incident pathway that triggers escalation to CRO and COO if the incident has not been resolved after 2 hours, and mandates customer communication.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Eight-Hour Board Notification Trigger
description: Decision point within the >4 hour incident pathway that mandates board update notification if the incident duration exceeds 8 hours.

name: Level 1–2 — IT Operations Short Duration Response
description: Frontline escalation tier for incidents lasting less than 1 hour with minimal customer impact. Handled by IT Operations with no escalation required and resolution target of 1 hour.

name: Level 2–3 — IT Operations and CTO Medium Duration Response
description: Supervisor-level escalation tier for incidents lasting 1–4 hours with significant customer impact. Handled by IT Operations and CTO, with escalation to CRO and COO after 2 hours and resolution target of 4 hours.

name: Level 4–5 — Executive Long Duration Response
description: Executive-level escalation tier for incidents lasting more than 4 hours with critical customer impact. Handled by CTO and CEO with immediate response, hourly updates, executive committee meeting, potential FCA notification, and board update if duration exceeds 8 hours.

name: IT Operations
description: Operations team responsible for handling and resolving operational incidents and system outages. Primary handler for incidents lasting less than 1 hour and co-handler for incidents lasting 1–4 hours.

name: Chief Technology Officer
description: Senior technology executive responsible for co-handling medium-duration incidents (1–4 hours) and leading response to long-duration incidents (>4 hours). Involved in escalation decisions and executive coordination.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Executive leader responsible for co-handling and directing response to long-duration incidents (>4 hours) with critical customer impact. Involved in immediate response coordination and executive committee meetings.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Risk management executive who receives escalation notification after 2 hours for medium-duration incidents (1–4 hours) and is involved in risk assessment and mitigation decisions.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Operations executive who receives escalation notification after 2 hours for medium-duration incidents (1–4 hours) and is involved in operational response coordination.
context: Escalate to CRO + COO after 2 hours

name: Executive Committee
description: Senior leadership body convened for incident review and decision-making when long-duration incidents (>4 hours) occur. Responsible for strategic response and regulatory coordination.

name: Regulatory Notification Compliance Gate
description: Mandatory compliance checkpoint requiring assessment and potential notification to the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for long-duration incidents (>4 hours) with critical customer impact. Determines whether regulatory reporting obligation is triggered.

name: Level 2 — Compliance and Department Manager Resolution
description: Escalation level for policy violations handled jointly by Compliance and Department Manager. Involves counseling and corrective action planning with a 30-day remediation timeline.

name: Level 3 — Compliance and Chief Risk Officer Resolution
description: Escalation level for low-impact regulatory rule breaches requiring immediate remediation within 5 days. Handled by Compliance and Chief Risk Officer with internal notification and remediation documentation.

name: Level 4–5 — Chief Risk Officer, Chief Executive Officer, and Legal Resolution
description: Highest escalation level for significant regulatory breaches requiring immediate escalation to regulatory authorities within 24 hours. Involves CRO, CEO, and Legal with FCA/PRA notification, board notification, and root cause analysis.

name: Compliance Staff
description: Compliance team responsible for handling violations across multiple escalation levels, from policy violations through regulatory breaches. Participates in counseling, remediation, and regulatory notification.

name: Department Manager
description: Department manager responsible for handling policy violations at Level 2, working jointly with Compliance to implement counseling and corrective action plans.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Chief Risk Officer responsible for escalation and remediation of regulatory breaches at Levels 3 and 4–5. Participates in immediate remediation decisions and regulatory contact.

name: Chief Executive Officer
description: Chief Executive Officer responsible for handling significant regulatory breaches at Level 4–5, including immediate escalation and regulatory contact decisions.

name: Legal Team
description: Legal team responsible for handling significant regulatory breaches at Level 4–5, supporting regulatory contact and notification processes.

name: Compliance Violation Severity Assessment
description: Decision gate that classifies compliance violations by severity level (Policy Violation, Low Impact Regulatory Breach, or Significant Regulatory Breach) to determine escalation path and response timeline.

name: Regulatory Compliance Notification
description: Mandatory regulatory reporting checkpoint for significant regulatory breaches requiring notification to FCA/PRA within 24 hours. Includes board notification and documentation of remediation.
context: Remediation: Root cause analysis + prevention plan

name: AML/KYC Issue Resolution Process
description: End-to-end procedure for identifying, escalating, and resolving AML/KYC compliance issues including missed documentation, PEP/sanctions hits, and suspicious transaction patterns. The process defines handler roles, escalation levels, required actions, and regulatory reporting timelines.

name: Missed KYC Documentation Handling
description: Immediate action to obtain missing KYC documentation before account processing can proceed. Assigned to Compliance handler at escalation Level 2 with same-day completion requirement.

name: PEP/Sanctions Hit Response
description: Immediate account freeze action triggered by a positive PEP or sanctions list match. Handled jointly by Compliance and Financial Crime teams at escalation Levels 3–4 with 4-hour response requirement and mandatory NCA notification.

name: Suspicious Transaction Pattern Investigation
description: Investigation and enhanced monitoring of suspicious transaction patterns detected on an account. Handled jointly by Financial Crime and Compliance at escalation Levels 2–3 with 5-day investigation timeline and potential SAR filing within 30 days if warranted.

name: Level 2 — Compliance Handler Resolution
description: Escalation Level 2 for AML/KYC issues including missed documentation and suspicious transaction patterns. Assigned to Compliance and Financial Crime handlers with same-day or 5-day investigation timelines respectively.

name: Level 3 — Financial Crime Escalation
description: Escalation Level 3 for PEP/sanctions hits and suspicious transaction patterns requiring enhanced investigation and potential regulatory reporting. Assigned to Financial Crime and Compliance teams with 4-hour to 5-day response timelines.

name: Level 4 — Executive Financial Crime Response
description: Escalation Level 4 for critical PEP/sanctions hits requiring immediate account freeze and NCA notification. Assigned to Compliance and Financial Crime teams with 4-hour response requirement.

name: Compliance Handler
description: Compliance team member responsible for handling missed KYC documentation issues, PEP/sanctions hits, and suspicious transaction pattern investigations. Acts as primary handler at Levels 2–4 with authority to freeze accounts and initiate regulatory reporting.

name: Financial Crime Team
description: Financial Crime team responsible for investigating PEP/sanctions hits and suspicious transaction patterns. Acts jointly with Compliance at Levels 2–4 with authority to recommend account freezes and SAR filings.

name: KYC Documentation Verification Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate verifying that all required KYC documentation has been collected and recorded before account processing proceeds. Failure triggers immediate escalation to Compliance handler with same-day remediation requirement.

name: PEP/Sanctions Screening Checkpoint
description: Mandatory regulatory gate screening customer identity against PEP and sanctions lists. Positive match triggers immediate account freeze, escalation to Levels 3–4, and mandatory NCA notification within 4 hours.
context: Reporting: NCA notification (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation)

name: Suspicious Transaction Monitoring Checkpoint
description: Mandatory compliance gate for detecting and investigating suspicious transaction patterns. Positive detection triggers enhanced monitoring, investigation within 5 days, and potential SAR filing within 30 days if warranted.

name: PEP Screening
description: Politically Exposed Person screening check performed as part of AML/KYC compliance. Positive match requires immediate account freeze and escalation to Financial Crime and Compliance teams with 4-hour response timeline.

name: Sanctions Screening
description: Sanctions list screening check performed as part of AML/KYC compliance. Positive match requires immediate account freeze, escalation to Levels 3–4, and NCA notification to the Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation within 4 hours.
context: Reporting: NCA notification (Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation)

name: Transaction Monitoring
description: Ongoing transaction monitoring to detect suspicious patterns on customer accounts. Positive detection triggers enhanced monitoring, investigation within 5 days, and potential SAR filing within 30 days.

name: Suspicious Activity Report Filing
description: Suspicious Activity Report filing obligation triggered by detection of suspicious transaction patterns. Filing must be completed within 30 days of investigation if warranted, with investigation period of 5 days.

name: KYC Documentation Collection
description: Know Your Customer documentation collection process. Failure to obtain required documentation triggers immediate escalation to Compliance handler with same-day remediation requirement before account processing can proceed.

name: KYC Documentation Completeness Gate
description: Decision gate determining whether all required KYC documentation has been collected. Pass path allows account processing to proceed; fail path triggers immediate escalation to Compliance handler for same-day documentation collection.

name: PEP/Sanctions Match Decision
description: Decision gate determining whether customer identity matches PEP or sanctions lists. Positive match triggers immediate account freeze, escalation to Levels 3–4, and NCA notification within 4 hours. Negative match allows normal processing.

name: Suspicious Transaction Pattern Detection Gate
description: Decision gate determining whether transaction patterns meet suspicious activity criteria. Positive detection triggers enhanced monitoring, 5-day investigation, and potential SAR filing within 30 days. Negative result allows normal monitoring to continue.

name: Level 1 — Manager Fee Reversal Authority
description: First-level authority for fee reversal decisions up to £1,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Director level.

name: Level 2 — Director Fee Reversal Authority
description: Second-level authority for fee reversal decisions exceeding £1,000. Escalates from Manager level.

name: Level 1 — Manager Complaint Resolution Authority
description: First-level authority for complaint resolution decisions up to £5,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Chief Complaints Officer.

name: Level 2 — Chief Complaints Officer Resolution Authority
description: Second-level authority for complaint resolution decisions exceeding £5,000. Escalates from Manager level.

name: Level 1 — Compliance Fraud Reimbursement Authority
description: First-level authority for fraud reimbursement decisions up to £10,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Chief Executive Officer.

name: Level 2 — Chief Executive Officer Fraud Reimbursement Authority
description: Second-level authority for fraud reimbursement decisions exceeding £10,000. Escalates from Compliance level.

name: Level 1 — Compliance Head KYC Exception Authority
description: First-level authority for KYC exception decisions with unlimited approval limit. Escalates to Chief Complaints Officer only when PEP or sanctions issues are identified.
context: KYC Exception | Compliance Head | Any | CRO if PEP/sanctions

name: Level 2 — Chief Complaints Officer KYC Exception Authority
description: Second-level authority for KYC exceptions involving PEP or sanctions screening issues. Escalates from Compliance Head level.
context: KYC Exception | Compliance Head | Any | CRO if PEP/sanctions

name: Level 1 — Product Manager Product Exception Authority
description: First-level authority for product exception decisions up to £50,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Board level.
context: Product Exception | Product Manager | £50,000 | Board if >£50k

name: Level 2 — Board Product Exception Authority
description: Second-level authority for product exception decisions exceeding £50,000. Escalates from Product Manager level.
context: Product Exception | Product Manager | £50,000 | Board if >£50k

name: Level 1 — Underwriter Lending Exception Authority
description: First-level authority for lending exception decisions within credit policy limits. Decisions involving policy violations escalate to Chief Complaints Officer.
context: Lending Exception | Underwriter | Credit policy | CRO if policy violation

name: Level 2 — Chief Complaints Officer Lending Exception Authority
description: Second-level authority for lending exception decisions involving credit policy violations. Escalates from Underwriter level.
context: Lending Exception | Underwriter | Credit policy | CRO if policy violation

name: Level 1 — Chief Technology Officer System Expenditure Authority
description: First-level authority for system expenditure decisions up to £50,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Chief Financial Officer.

name: Level 2 — Chief Financial Officer System Expenditure Authority
description: Second-level authority for system expenditure decisions exceeding £50,000. Escalates from Chief Technology Officer level.

name: Level 1 — Department Head Vendor Contract Authority
description: First-level authority for vendor contract decisions up to £100,000. Decisions exceeding this limit escalate to Chief Executive Officer.
context: Vendor Contract | Department Head | £100,000 | CEO if >£100k

name: Level 2 — Chief Executive Officer Vendor Contract Authority
description: Second-level authority for vendor contract decisions exceeding £100,000. Escalates from Department Head level.
context: Vendor Contract | Department Head | £100,000 | CEO if >£100k

name: Escalation Best Practices
description: A procedural guideline defining the conditions and triggers that mandate immediate escalation of banking operational issues. The process establishes seven distinct escalation criteria covering financial, regulatory, reputational, and operational dimensions.
context: Financial impact exceeds your approval limit

name: Financial Impact Approval Limit Check
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when the financial impact of an issue exceeds the decision-maker's delegated approval authority. This is the first escalation criterion in the best practices framework.
context: Financial impact exceeds your approval limit

name: Regulatory or Compliance Implication Gate
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when an issue carries regulatory or compliance implications. This ensures that matters with potential regulatory exposure are elevated to appropriate authority.

name: Reputational Risk Assessment Gate
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when an issue poses reputational risk to the organization. This ensures visibility and management of matters that could affect the bank's public standing or brand.

name: Customer Relationship Risk Gate
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when an issue threatens the customer relationship. This ensures that matters affecting customer retention or satisfaction receive appropriate management attention.

name: Authority and Expertise Sufficiency Check
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when the handling officer lacks the necessary authority or expertise to resolve an issue. This ensures that complex or specialized matters are directed to qualified personnel.

name: Issue Clarity and Complexity Assessment Gate
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when an issue is unclear or complex. This ensures that ambiguous or multifaceted matters receive appropriate senior review before resolution.

name: Resolution Timeout Gate
description: A decision gate that triggers escalation when an issue remains unresolved after 24 hours. This ensures that stalled matters are elevated to prevent further delay and customer impact.

name: Escalation Procedure
description: A structured end-to-end procedure for escalating issues within the organization. The process requires documentation of the issue, direct contact with the escalation authority via email and phone, provision of contextual background and recommendations, prompt response to authority questions, immediate implementation of decisions, and stakeholder notification.
context: Document Issue: Summary, timeline, financial impact, efforts so far
Contact Escalation Authority: Email + phone call (don't wait)
Implement Decision: Once authority decides, execute immediately

name: Issue Documentation
description: The initial step in the escalation procedure where the issue is formally documented with a summary, timeline of events, financial impact assessment, and a record of efforts undertaken to date.
context: Document Issue: Summary, timeline, financial impact, efforts so far

name: Escalation Authority Contact
description: The step where the escalation authority is contacted via both email and phone call without delay. The instruction emphasizes not waiting and using both communication channels to ensure immediate attention.
context: Contact Escalation Authority: Email + phone call (don't wait)

name: Context and Recommendation Provision
description: The step where background information, options that have been considered, and a specific recommendation are provided to the escalation authority to support their decision-making.
context: Provide Context: Background, options considered, recommendation

name: Authority Response Awaiting
description: The step where the escalating party waits for the authority to respond, with the expectation that the authority may ask clarifying questions that must be answered promptly.
context: Wait for Response: Authority may ask questions (respond promptly)

name: Decision Implementation
description: The step where the decision made by the escalation authority is executed immediately upon receipt, without delay.
context: Implement Decision: Once authority decides, execute immediately

name: Stakeholder Notification
description: The final step in the escalation procedure where all relevant stakeholders—including the customer, team members, and manager—are informed of the outcome and actions taken.
context: Update Stakeholders: Inform customer, team, manager

name: Escalation Authority
description: The designated authority responsible for receiving escalated issues, reviewing the documentation and context provided, asking clarifying questions as needed, and making final decisions on issue resolution.
context: Contact Escalation Authority: Email + phone call (don't wait)

name: Escalating Staff Member
description: The staff member or team responsible for initiating the escalation, documenting the issue, contacting the authority, providing context and recommendations, responding to questions, implementing decisions, and updating stakeholders.
context: Document Issue: Summary, timeline, financial impact, efforts so far
Contact Escalation Authority: Email + phone call (don't wait)
Provide Context: Background, options considered, recommendation

name: Customer
description: The customer who is affected by the escalated issue and must be informed of the outcome and actions taken as part of stakeholder notification.
context: Update Stakeholders: Inform customer, team, manager

name: Team Member
description: Team members who are stakeholders in the escalated issue and must be informed of the resolution and actions taken.
context: Update Stakeholders: Inform customer, team, manager

name: Manager
description: The manager who is a stakeholder in the escalated issue and must be informed of the outcome and actions taken.
context: Update Stakeholders: Inform customer, team, manager

name: Escalation Procedure
description: A procedural framework governing when and how operational issues should be escalated to higher authority levels. The procedure establishes best practices for escalation communication, including requirements to provide complete context, include recommendations, maintain responsiveness, and follow decisions without second-guessing. It also defines constraints on escalation, prohibiting premature escalation before attempting resolution at the current level, re-escalation of already-decided matters, and escalation of trivial issues.
context: DO provide complete context (don't make escalation authority investigate)
DO include recommendation (show you've thought it through)
DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level
DON'T escalate trivial issues (know your authority limit)

name: Context Provision for Escalation
description: The step of providing complete context to the escalation authority to enable informed decision-making without requiring the authority to conduct their own investigation.
context: DO provide complete context (don't make escalation authority investigate)

name: Recommendation Formulation for Escalation
description: The step of including a reasoned recommendation when escalating an issue, demonstrating that the escalating party has already considered the matter and formed a view on the appropriate resolution.
context: DO include recommendation (show you've thought it through)

name: Responsive Communication During Escalation
description: The step of maintaining responsiveness to questions and requests from the escalation authority, ensuring timely answers to support the escalation decision-making process.
context: DO be responsive (answer authority questions quickly)

name: Decision Implementation After Escalation
description: The step of implementing the escalation authority's decision without second-guessing or re-evaluating the decision once it has been made.

name: Resolution Attempt at Current Level
description: The mandatory step of attempting to resolve an issue at the current authority level before escalating to a higher level, establishing a prerequisite condition for escalation.
context: DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level

name: Escalation Necessity Gate
description: A decision gate determining whether an issue should be escalated to higher authority or resolved at the current level. The gate enforces that escalation should only occur after resolution attempts at the current level have been exhausted, and that trivial issues within the current authority's limit should not be escalated.
context: DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level
DON'T escalate trivial issues (know your authority limit)

name: Re-escalation Prohibition Gate
description: A decision gate preventing re-escalation of matters that have already been decided by higher authority, unless material circumstances have changed since the original decision.
context: DON'T escalate again if already decided (only if circumstances change)

name: Escalating Staff Member
description: The operational staff member responsible for initiating escalation, who must attempt resolution at their level first, provide complete context and recommendations, and remain responsive to the escalation authority's questions.
context: DO provide complete context (don't make escalation authority investigate)
DON'T escalate until you've tried resolution at your level

name: Escalation Authority
description: The higher-level authority responsible for receiving escalations, making decisions on escalated matters, and whose decisions must be implemented by the escalating staff member without second-guessing.

name: Emergency Escalation
description: A 24/7 emergency escalation procedure for critical operational incidents including system outages, security incidents, regulatory issues, and customer crises. The process routes calls to designated on-call personnel based on incident type, with contact numbers and escalation paths maintained by the Operations team.
context: On-Call List: Maintained by Operations, updated monthly

name: System Outage Escalation
description: Escalation step for system outage incidents, requiring immediate contact with IT On-Call personnel via dedicated phone line.

name: Security Incident Escalation
description: Escalation step for security incidents, requiring immediate contact with Security On-Call personnel via dedicated phone line.

name: Regulatory Issue Escalation
description: Escalation step for regulatory issues, requiring immediate contact with the Chief Risk Officer (CRO) via mobile phone registered with the operations team.
context: Regulatory issue: Call CRO Mobile (registered with ops team)

name: Customer Crisis Escalation
description: Escalation step for customer crises, requiring immediate contact with CEO or COO via phone numbers registered with the operations team.
context: Customer crisis: Call CEO/COO (registered with ops team)

name: IT On-Call
description: On-call IT personnel responsible for responding to system outage emergencies 24/7. Reachable via dedicated phone line 0800-888-TECH.

name: Security On-Call
description: On-call security personnel responsible for responding to security incidents 24/7. Reachable via dedicated phone line 0800-888-SECU.

name: Chief Risk Officer
description: Executive responsible for regulatory escalations, available on-call via mobile phone registered with the operations team.
context: Regulatory issue: Call CRO Mobile (registered with ops team)

name: Chief Executive Officer / Chief Operating Officer
description: Senior executives responsible for customer crisis escalations, available on-call via phone numbers registered with the operations team.
context: Customer crisis: Call CEO/COO (registered with ops team)

name: Operations Team
description: Team responsible for maintaining and updating the on-call list monthly, and registering contact details for CRO, CEO, and COO escalation contacts.
context: On-Call List: Maintained by Operations, updated monthly

name: Level 1 — IT On-Call System Outage Response
description: First-line escalation level for system outage incidents, handled by IT On-Call personnel available 24/7 via phone 0800-888-TECH.

name: Level 1 — Security On-Call Incident Response
description: First-line escalation level for security incidents, handled by Security On-Call personnel available 24/7 via phone 0800-888-SECU.

name: Level 2 — Chief Risk Officer Regulatory Escalation
description: Executive escalation level for regulatory issues, handled by the Chief Risk Officer via registered mobile phone.
context: Regulatory issue: Call CRO Mobile (registered with ops team)

name: Level 2 — CEO/COO Customer Crisis Response
description: Executive escalation level for customer crises, handled by CEO or COO via registered phone numbers.
context: Customer crisis: Call CEO/COO (registered with ops team)

name: Level 1 Escalation
description: First-line escalation tier with 1-hour acknowledgment time, 24-hour investigation window, and same-day decision requirement. Represents the initial escalation point for operational issues.

name: Level 2 Escalation
description: Second-tier escalation with 2-hour acknowledgment, 2-day investigation period, and 3-day decision timeline. Represents supervisor or manager-level resolution authority.

name: Level 3 Escalation
description: Third-tier escalation with 4-hour acknowledgment, 3-day investigation period, and 5-day decision timeline. Represents department-head level authority for complex cases.

name: Level 4 Escalation
description: Fourth-tier escalation with 2-hour acknowledgment, 1-day investigation period, and 2-day decision timeline. Represents expedited executive-level resolution with compressed timelines.

name: Level 5 Escalation
description: Fifth-tier escalation with 1-hour acknowledgment, 24-hour investigation period, and 3-day decision timeline with provision for immediate decision on critical matters. Represents highest escalation authority.
context: Level 5 | 1 hour | 24 hours | 3 days (or immediate if critical)

name: Escalation Reporting Process
description: A formal reporting and review procedure that captures escalation metrics monthly and conducts quarterly reviews with governance committees. The process tracks escalation volumes by level, resolution times, root causes, and systemic issues to identify trends and drive process improvements.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations
Audit committee notified of regulatory escalations

name: Monthly Escalation Report Compilation
description: A monthly data collection and reporting step that aggregates escalation metrics including total count by level, average resolution time, common reasons for escalation, identified systemic issues, and trend analysis.

name: Quarterly Escalation Review
description: A quarterly governance review step where escalation trends are discussed with relevant committees, regulatory escalations are reported to audit oversight, and process improvements are considered based on identified patterns.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations
Audit committee notified of regulatory escalations

name: Board Risk Committee
description: The governance body responsible for receiving notification of Level 5 escalations and reviewing escalation trends as part of the quarterly review process.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations

name: Audit Committee
description: The governance body responsible for receiving notification of regulatory escalations and participating in the quarterly review of escalation trends and process improvements.
context: Audit committee notified of regulatory escalations

name: Level 5 Escalation
description: The highest escalation level in the escalation matrix, requiring notification to the Board Risk Committee during quarterly reviews.
context: Board Risk Committee notified of Level 5 escalations

name: Department Contacts and Authorities
description: A reference document containing department contact information and authority assignments relevant to operational procedures.

name: Complaint Escalation Policy
description: A policy document detailing the escalation procedures and handling requirements for customer complaints.

name: Operational Risk Incident Escalation Policy
description: A policy document defining the escalation framework and procedures for operational risk incidents and exceptions.

name: Escalation Matrix Document
description: A versioned operational document defining escalation procedures and approval authority levels. The document has undergone three revisions since initial creation, with the most recent update adding 24/7 emergency contact information and prior updates to approval limits.

name: Chief Operating Officer
description: Executive role responsible for authoring and maintaining the escalation matrix document. The COO has authored all three versions of the document, including updates to approval limits and emergency contact procedures.
context: Change | Added 24/7 emergency contacts | Author | COO
Change | Updated approval limits | Author | COO
